title: Failure of three-colorability
statement: Let $v$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $G$ be a graph on the vertex set $\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$, encoded by assigning a Boolean value to each two-element vertex set. The non-three-colorability property of $G$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly when $G$ cannot be properly colored with three colors.
caveat: The supplied snippet does not include the definition of graph colorability or how Boolean edge values determine adjacency.
